html.body: Date: 2025-03-17 Remarks Claims 1-20 are currently pending in this Application. Applicant appreciates the recognition of allowed claims 11-16. By this Amendment, claims 1 and 6-8 are amended, claims 17-20 are cancelled, and new claims 21-24 are added. After entry of this Amendment, claims 1- 16 and 21-24 will be pending. Reconsideration in view of the above amendments to the claims and the following remarks is respectfully requested.Objection to Claims 3-5 Claims 3-5 are objected to as being dependent on a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form. Applicant appreciates the recognition of allowable subject matter in claims 3-5. As presented below, independent claim 1 has been amended to recite allowable subject matter. Because claims 3-5 depend from an independent claim, which has been amended to recite allowable subject matter, withdrawal of the objection to claims 3-5 is respectfully requested.Rejection of Claims 1-2 and 6-10 Under § 102/103 In the Office Action, claims 1-2 and 6-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being anticipated by U.S. Patent No. 9,296,469 ("Santini") or, in the alternative, rendered obvious over Santini in view of U.S. Patent No. 3,333,792 ("Alvarez-Calderon").These rejections are respectfully traversed. Nevertheless, to help expedite prosecution of this application, claim 1 has been amended.Independent claim 1 has been amended to recite a wing that comprises, in part, "a wing tip", "an upper wing-tip panel coupled to the wing tip", and "a lower wing-tip panel coupled to the wing tip". Claim 1 has been further amended to recite "the upper wing-tip panel is pivotable, relative to the wing tip, and extends vertically upward from the wing tip when the wing tip is in the retracted position" and "the lower wing-tip panel is pivotable, relative to the wing tip, and extends vertically downward from the wing tip when the wing tip is in the retracted position".Support for the amendments to claim 1 can be found in at least Paragraphs 14 and 54, and Figures 5 and 13, of the present application as originally filed.Santini does not teach, disclose, or suggest an upper wing-tip panel and a lower wing-tip panel, as now recited in claim 1. On Page 6 of the Office Action, the Office Action identifies a first surface and a second surface of a drop portion as disclosing upper and lower wing-tip panels. However, as shown in Figure 12, the first and second surfaces shown as blocks in Figure 4 are actually two surfaces of the same panel (e.g., surfaces 1212, 1214 of drop portion 1206).Accordingly, Santini does not even teach two separate panels, let alone two panels where one of the panels "extends vertically upward from the wing tip when the wing tip is in the retracted position" and the other panel "extends vertically downward from the wing tip when the wing tip is in the retracted position". For at least this reason, Santini does not anticipate claim 1 and withdrawal of the anticipation rejection of claim 1 is respectfully requested.Alvarez-Calderon does not overcome the deficiencies of Santini. For example, Alvarez- Calderon does not disclose at least "the upper wing-tip panel is pivotable, relative to the wing tip, and extends vertically upward from the wing tip when the wing tip is in the retracted position" and "the lower wing-tip panel is pivotable, relative to the wing tip, and extends vertically downward from the wing tip when the wing tip is in the retracted position". In view of the foregoing, the applied combination of Santini and Alvarez-Calderon does not render obvious independent claim 1. For this reason, withdrawal of the obviousness rejection of claim 1 is respectfully requested.Claims 2 and 6-10, being dependent upon base claim 1, are not anticipated by Santini or rendered obvious over Santini in view of Alvarez-Calderon for at least the same reasons as claim 1, as well as in view of the respective additional features recited in claims 2 and 6-10.Accordingly, withdrawal of the anticipation and obviousness rejections of claims 2 and 6-10 is respectfully requested.Conclusion Based on the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that the current claims are drawn to allowable subject matter and that the application is in condition for allowance. Any amendment to or cancellation of a claim by this Amendment is not a concession that the claim, prior to amendment or cancellation, did not contain patentable subject matter over the applied art. Rather, any claim amendment or cancellation in this Amendment is only for facilitating expeditious prosecution of the application. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue the subject matter of any amended or cancelled claim prior to amendment or cancellation in one or more related patent applications. Should the Examiner believe that anything further, such as amendments to the claims, be necessary to place this application in better condition for allowance, the Examiner is requested to contact Applicant's representative by telephone.Respectfully submitted, /Bryan J.
